newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian share prices seen stable, market quiet.
newsitem.headline: Estonian share prices seen stable, market quiet.

text.p: Estonian share trade dipped on Tuesday and dealers said prices seemed to be at a fair level for the time being.
Overall volume on the main official list was just two million kroons, versus 5.8 million kroons on Monday. The Tallinn stock exchange index dipped 0.25 percent to 97.74.
The secondary market turned over more shares than the main list, registering volume of 2.1 million kroons.
"It seems to me that prices are at a stable level and that is why trading is low," said Tonu Pekk, head of equities at leading bank Hansapank.
Hansapank, usually a well-traded stock, saw volume of just 600,000 kroons and it ended at 94.30 kroons versus 94.47.
"If trading in Hansapank is low then it shows that the market is slack," said Savings Bank dealer Charlie Viikberg.
The most traded share on the free market was the Tallinna Kaubamaja department store with turnover of nearly 800,000 kroons. It eased to 53 kroons from 53.30 kroons.
"The market is lacking money and small investors are directing their interest to the over-the-counter market," said Tallinna Pank trader Toomas Tsopp.
"Possible gains in the main list are fairly low but the free market shares are very attractive," he added.
